description: An oscillator giving sine, triangle, sawtooth and pulse from one phase at the same time, with a white noise source beside them, and frequency, amplitude and pulse width modulation inputs

params.text: Sets the frequency, five octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the duty cycle of the SQR output, an even square at the centre and a narrowing pulse towards either end; the other four outputs take no notice of it
Attenuates and inverts the pulse width modulation voltage before it shifts the duty cycle of the SQR output, and at the centre that voltage changes nothing
Scales the frequency modulation voltage, 5V moving the frequency by 261.63Hz at the clockwise end; turned counter-clockwise past the centre it inverts the modulation
Sets how far the amplitude modulation voltage controls the level, from no effect at the counter-clockwise end to the voltage setting the level outright at the clockwise end

inputs.text: Transposes the oscillator at one volt per octave, added to the FREQ knob
Shifts the duty cycle of the SQR output, 10V moving it by half the full width at the clockwise end of its attenuverter, and the result is held between 1% and 99%
Modulates the frequency, scaled by the FM knob; the shift is added to the frequency rather than multiplied by it, so a large enough negative voltage runs the oscillator backwards
Resets the oscillator's phase to zero on each rising edge past 1V, which is hard sync, and the SYNC lamp flashes for 0.15 seconds each time
Sets the level of the SIN, TRI, SAW and SQR outputs, scaled by the AM knob, with 10V full and 0V silent at the clockwise end of that knob; the NOIS output is left alone

outputs.text: A triangle wave at ±5V, its two corners rounded by polyBLAMP so they do not alias
A sawtooth wave at ±5V, its step smoothed by polyBLEP so it does not alias
A pulse wave at ±5V whose duty cycle comes from the PW knob and the pulse width modulation input, with both its edges smoothed by polyBLEP
White noise at ±5V, a fresh random value every sample, unrelated to the oscillator's frequency and phase and untouched by the amplitude modulation

notes: the four oscillator waveforms come from a single phase, so they are always at the same frequency and all restart together at a sync pulse
a waveform is worked out only while something is patched into its output, so outputs left empty cost no processing
the FM lamp brightens with the frequency modulation voltage multiplied by the depth set on the FM knob, and stays dark while the FM jack is empty

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.4:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads full level, the modulation switched off.
